title: Nine Paces Across the Square
subtitle: 中心与中央 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 中心与中央（社会服务与人际沟通·城镇与场所）
meta: 主题语境：中心与中央（社会服务与人际沟通·城镇与场所）　|　核心词汇：centre　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 centre 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1950 my mother was sent to find ① centre she could not mark, and she said the finding was the whole of the lesson. The ② centre, meaning the middle and not the building, was nine paces across and was found by whoever came last; centre, she said, is the only thing in a town that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ centre in that town had the same square, and the ④ centre at the end, meaning the one the planners kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever found properly. Centre, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ centre was the whole of the plan, meaning the purpose it held and not the middle. The ⑥ centre, meaning the purpose and not any of that, is the only thing in a plan that everybody serves and nobody questions; centre, he said, is either something you find or the only word that means both a middle and a purpose. She said the purpose is the part they remember.

By 1965 the ⑦ centre had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the square. The ⑧ centre of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine paces and eleven years of finding; centre, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ centre I remember is the one at the end, which was found in 1970 and is still described as the busiest in the county. A ⑩ centre, my grandmother said in 1975, is the only thing that improves by being found; every centre, she said, is a purpose that has agreed to look like a middle. She said the purpose was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 中心（指那个中心点本身，与整座建筑相对）
C. 固定搭配：find a centre 找到中心
D. n. 中心（指镇上每一处）
E. n. 中心（指末尾那一处）
F. n. 核心（抽象：它承载的那个目的）
G. n. 那个目的（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The centre, meaning the middle and not the building
centre was the whole of the plan
the centre had become a number in a report
The centre of the whole thing
A centre, my grandmother said in 1975

answers.why: find a centre 意为“找到中心”，1950 年母亲被派去找她标不出的那个中心。
centre 意为“中心、中央”，指那个中心点本身而不是整座建筑，横跨九步，由最后来的人找到。
centre 指镇上每一处中心，每一处都是同样的广场。
centre 指末尾那一处（规划者保留的那一处），是唯一有人认真找过的。
centre 意为“核心”，抽象指它承载的那个目的，父亲说 centre 就是那份规划的全部。
centre 为抽象用法，指那个目的本身，是一份规划里人人都服务、却没人质疑的东西。
centre 意为“中心、中央”，到 1965 年这处 centre 成了报告里的一个数字。
centre 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九步与十一年的寻找。
centre 意为“中心”，我记得的是末尾那一处，1970 年被找到，至今仍被说成全县最热闹的。
centre 为抽象总称，祖母说一处中心是唯一会因为被认真寻找而变好的东西。
